record.paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For each of the 34 orders at most 20000 for which the number of finite groups has been enumerated but the groups themselves have not been explicitly constructed, can one construct representative groups for every isomorphism type? The orders include 2^10; the 32 orders of the forms 2^9 * p for odd prime p, 2^8 * p * q for p in {3, 5, 7} and q prime different from 2 and p, 2^7 * 3^2 * p for p prime different from 2 and 3, and the specific orders 8640, 9600, 13440, 16320, 17280, 19440; and the additional order 12500.

artifact.status_search_result: Constructing the 49,487,365,422 groups of order 1024 explicitly remains impractical and is not included in the GAP SmallGroups library (version 1.5.4, July 2024); the library still excludes order 1024. Counts have been verified/corrected by recent cohomological enumeration methods, but a complete explicit list of representatives is not provided. For several of the other listed orders, partial constructions have appeared, but no comprehensive explicit construction covering all 34 orders is known.

status_evidence.title: On the number of groups of order 1024
status_evidence.claim: The number of groups of order 1024 has been enumerated, but explicit construction of representatives is impractical.
